headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced for this MinerU–RisingWave pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and expose an MCP server, so attacker-controlled document content could reach downstream consumers. RisingWave has no documented input bridge from MinerU, and no shared channel is shown, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and likely manual or orchestrated. The uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into RisingWave SQL, UDFs, or ingestion jobs without sanitization, injection risk exists.
IF an MCP or API bridge forwards MinerU text into RisingWave automation, attacker-controlled content can influence downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable any automatic copy/paste bridge between MinerU and RisingWave.
Require a human review step before using extracted text in SQL or ETL jobs.
Strip instruction-like text from MinerU outputs before downstream use.
Use a separate workspace or queue for untrusted document extractions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to MinerU outputs and enforce them in RisingWave ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, while RisingWave has no documented data classes or egress. There is no evidence of a shared filesystem or authenticated principal, so leakage is not established. However, if the pair is wired through a shared workspace, extracted document contents could flow into RisingWave processing.
conditions: IF MinerU writes extracted content into a shared directory that RisingWave reads, document data can leak across the pair.
IF RisingWave is configured to ingest MinerU outputs containing sensitive documents, those contents become part of downstream processing.
mitigations: Keep MinerU and RisingWave on separate storage volumes.
Restrict RisingWave inputs to approved, non-sensitive datasets.
Review and redact sensitive fields before ingestion.
Turn off any automatic export from MinerU into shared locations.
requires-engineering: implement access controls and audit logs on the handoff path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells; RisingWave exposes no overlapping write surface in the profile. With no shared mutable resource or locking issue documented, there is no plausible write-conflict pathway to assess.
conditions: IF RisingWave is deployed with an undocumented writable shared directory, conflict risk would need re-evaluation.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate directories and databases.
Avoid mounting the same writable volume into both systems.
Document any shared mutable resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text and structured document content, and RisingWave is a data-engineering system that could consume those outputs in pipelines. The pairwise pathway exists if RisingWave treats MinerU output as authoritative without validation. Because no verification step is documented, uncertainty favors the higher severity over low.
conditions: IF RisingWave pipelines use MinerU extraction results as source-of-truth without schema or quality checks, cascading errors can propagate.
IF MinerU OCR or table extraction is imperfect and RisingWave materializes the result, downstream analytics may be wrong.
mitigations: Add validation checks before loading MinerU output into RisingWave.
Compare extracted fields against source documents for a sample set.
Flag low-confidence OCR or table parses for manual review.
Use staging tables before production materialized views.
requires-engineering: add automated reconciliation between source documents and ingested rows.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. MinerU is open-source and offline-oriented, while RisingWave shows no compliance-specific claims in the profile, so a compliance breach is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF either deployment routes regulated data to an unapproved environment, compliance must be reassessed.
mitigations: Classify the data before processing.
Keep regulated data out of unapproved deployments.
Record retention and deletion settings for both systems.
